scope: Narrow read-only review of value disclosure, execution and target scope. No H dispatch, Python execution, target read or runtime authority assertion.
observed_controls: The only data-path file open is the fixed TARGET using O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC|O_NONBLOCK; fd/path identity is checked before and after.
The exact prior device/inode/mode/nlink/size/mtime_ns/ctime_ns/SHA is compared before AST parsing. Raw integer timestamp tokens match without JS Number roundtrip.
Only the inspector's fixed standard-library imports execute. The target is UTF-8 decoded and ast.parse'd, never imported, evaluated, executed, compiled to executable bytecode, or spawned.
Constant.value is never accessed. Source lines, exception text/args/reprs, docstrings, literal values, argv element values and environment values are not emitted.
AST names emitted from the target are limited to fixed observed call/import/path-name allowlists. Other names are internal lookup keys only and are replaced with null/unknown in output.
The env keyword is recorded only as present; its expression is not followed by origin(). All kwargs not explicitly categorized are omitted.
Bounded origin traversal reports syntax/locations, does not resolve referenced filesystem paths or open them, and marks receiver type/runtime dataflow as unproved.
Dynamic/unknown calls are kept unknown; file-method labels and path-join syntax do not establish actual runtime object types or grants.
The prior sampled filesystem stability limitation and explicit ordinary_execution_authority_proven=false/runtime_owner_custody_observed=false remain.
limitations: This is source review of the inspector, not a Python parse/test or an actual target observation.
The fixed same-file identity check does not provide a filesystem lock or a process/deployment authority.
Global AST call-shape/count observation can describe calls nested within any expression, including an env expression; no argument value is exported and no runtime value is evaluated.
